newsitem.title: HONG KONG: K&P Int'l ends debut below issue price.
newsitem.headline: K&P Int'l ends debut below issue price.

text.p: Shares of electronics firm K&P International Holdings Ltd ended their trading debut on Thursday at HK$0.93 per share, below their issue price of HK$1.00.
Brokers said stop-loss selling quickly emerged as the shares dived below their issue price.
K&P shares moved in a range of HK$0.92 to HK$1.05, with 39.63 million shares worth HK$39.08 million traded.
Analysts said the fall was expected due to the relatively low subscription rate to the initial public offering (IPO).
K&P offered 55 million new shares at HK$1.00 each in its IPO, with one warrant to be issued for every five shares. The IPO was 13.1 times subscribed.

"A relatively high listing PE (price to earnings multiple) of about 6.5 times compared with its counterparts led to anticipation of limited room on the upside and that made the stock less attractive," said Alex Wong, research analyst at Dharmala Securities.
Electronic products maker Tomorrow International Holdings Ltd was trading at a price to earnings multiple of about 5.48 times.
Brokers said they expected followthrough stop-loss selling to put pressure on K&P's share price in the short run.
K&P makes conductive silicone rubber keypads, electronic calculators, alarm clocks and plastic products.
